summary: You take the proseminar twice, the colloquium, the theory and methods sequences, four survey courses, SOC 300, six quarters of SOC 394 and the SOC 386 practicum, and 60 units of Sociology coursework not counting workshops, independent study or directed research, within the 135 units of the PhD. Required courses need a letter grade (unless offered only S/NC) and a B+ or better; the 60 units count only letter-graded courses, and the B+ on the ones no rule requires is checked by hand. Workshops each quarter, colloquium enrollment every quarter, the qualifying exams, the publishable paper, presentations, prospectus, candidacy, oral exam and dissertation are checked by hand.

program.why: Grading: "Students are expected to enroll in all required courses and any courses that count toward the minimum required 60 units of Sociology coursework for a letter grade unless that option is not available. Students must receive a B+in any required courses and any courses that count toward the minimum required 60 units of Sociology coursework." The rule covers required courses and the 60 units, not every course toward the university's 135, so the letter grade and B+ are set on the required rules and the 60-unit total counts only letter-graded courses. Courses offered only S/NC count with an S.
